name: USB-A (USB 2.0)
description: The classic flat rectangular USB host connector. Four contacts: 5 V power, a differential data pair (D+/D-), and ground. The two power contacts (1, 4) are longer than the data contacts, so on insertion power mates first and breaks last, making hot-plugging safe. USB 3.x Type-A adds a second row of 5 SuperSpeed contacts further back but stays backward compatible with these four.

contacts.name: VBUS
contacts.description: +5 V bus power (red wire); 500 mA default on USB 2.0, more with BC/charging

variants: USB 3.x Type-A ('SuperSpeed', often blue): same 4 pins here plus 5 recessed contacts (2 SS pairs + GND) in a second row further inside the shell; fully backward compatible.
Wire colours (red/white/green/black) are the standard USB convention but cheap cables lie, meter before trusting them.
gotchas: Pin order is VBUS, D-, D+, GND (1-4). The two power pins (1 & 4) are physically longer so power connects first and disconnects last on hot-plug.
The D+/D- pair is a 90-ohm differential line; keep it matched-length and away from noise or high-speed USB fails intermittently.
VBUS is 5 V but current depends on negotiation: 500 mA (USB 2.0), 900 mA (USB 3.0), up to 1.5 A with BC1.2; a device pulling more than the port allows just browns out.
notes: USB-A 4-pin pinout per the USB 2.0 spec; universal and unchanged since USB 1.0.
